Four replies (c4-c7), each with a parentId pointing at c0-c3 and a non-empty anchor.startBlockId (p3/p12/p22/p30); each shows in read --comments as its own [^cN] footnote with a ↳ cN marker

The agent finalized all 10 tracked changes in one track-changes apply call (after a dry-run) and posted all four replies plus both resolves in one comments reply --batch, which is the intended batched review path

The agent had to cross-reference both outputs to find every handle.
defects.evidence: Agent deadEnds and frictions. The output is not affected.

defects.what: The apply --dry-run preview uses XML-level action labels ('unwrap'/'delete') instead of accept/reject outcomes, and labels an accepted pPrChange as 'delete'
defects.evidence: Agent deadEnds. This is a UX problem only.

defects.evidence: Agent friction. The agent worked around it with a per-line author key, so the output is unaffected.

notes: Clean pass on every rubric item. The baseline markdown is the accepted-view read, so the textual diff shows only the $100 restore and §11 reinstated with the renumbering that follows. The table cell 'Net 90 after final acceptance' and the 'Sections 4 through 12' cross-reference are pre-existing and were never tracked changes. Resolved comments still appear in Word's margin render, which is normal Word behavior.
weakAgentStruggle: Low. The agent took the efficient batched path: read, then list, then one apply and one reply --batch. It still had to manually work out the three handles (tc7/tc8/tc9) that make up the §11 deletion, because track-changes list does not group a pure deletion and the read view omits markers for tc4/tc8. The dry-run labels were confusing but did not mislead it.
